elements.char: Discussion
elements.label: text

elements.char: In this work, we have proposed a novel reconstruction method, named CINENet, for 3D cardiac CINE MRI
elements.label: text

elements.char: based on a deep learning network which enables highly accelerated imaging sequences. We found that employing
elements.label: text

elements.char: the proposed CINENet allows for 3D isotropic CINE acquisition in a single breath-hold of <
elements.label: text

elements.char: 10 s scan time with
elements.label: text

elements.char: 5 s reconstruction time. We observed that CINENet can provide visually improved images over CS for these
elements.label: text

elements.char: high acceleration factors while enabling a 22-fold faster acquisition than conventional 2D CINE and a 24-fold
elements.label: text

elements.char: faster reconstruction than CS facilitating clinical translation. Our qualitative and quantitative results indicate
elements.label: text

elements.char: good agreement of 3D CINE with conventional 2D CINE, which, whether confirmed in larger patient studies,
elements.label: text

elements.char: will pave the way for clinically grounded applications.
elements.label: text

elements.char: Rapid assessment of cardiac function by cardiac CINE plays a vital role in patient monitoring and staging
elements.label: text

elements.char: of cardiovascular or cardio-oncological diseases. Visualizing cardiac anatomy and function in 3D can help in
elements.label: text

elements.char: the diagnosis of congenital heart diseases, for the detection of regional wall motion abnormalities or impaired
elements.label: text

elements.char: ejection fraction. A 3D isotropic imaging resolution with Cartesian sampling allows for reformats in arbitrary
elements.label: text

elements.char: orientations without loss of resolution avoiding multiple breath-hold acquisitions in double-oblique orientations.
elements.label: text

elements.char: This leads to more efficient workflow and improved patient comfort.
elements.label: text

elements.char: We have reported a novel deep learning reconstruction that works with multi-coil and complex-valued 4D
elements.label: text

elements.char: cardiac phases) data. The proposed architecture reflects an unrolled optimization algorithm with complex-
elements.label: text

elements.char: valued convolutions and activation functions and intermittent data consistency blocks to properly handle the
elements.label: text

elements.char: input data. We accomplish computationally efficient spatio-temporal information sharing by cascaded 3D spatial
elements.label: text

elements.char: and 1D temporal convolutional kernels. CINENet incorporates coil sensitivity maps to provide a multi-coil
elements.label: text

elements.char: reconstruction. We obtained qualitatively good images which indicates the capability of the proposed network to
elements.label: text

elements.char: utilize spatio-temporal redundancies. Training for various acceleration factors and temporal resolutions improved
elements.label: text

elements.char: generalizability to different inputs. We observed that the selected acceleration factors for training are sufficient
elements.label: text

elements.char: to simulate the expected levels of aliasing artifact appearance. Reconstructions of prospectively undersampled
elements.label: text

elements.char: acquisitions with larger acceleration factors were possible indicating enough diversity in the training database.
elements.label: text

elements.char: Our results show that data-adaptive training of a sparsifying transformation for changing imaging conditions
elements.label: text

elements.char: (temporal resolution, accelerations, subjects) demonstrates to be more generalizable and robust than a fixed
elements.label: text

elements.char: sparsity basis and regularization parameters as in CS. In case of CS, subject- and undersampling factor-dependent
elements.label: text

elements.char: regularization parameters are conceivable. Here, the selected CS regularization parameters were optimized to fit
elements.label: text

elements.char: all subjects and accelerations. Furthermore, we observed that the network generalized for different field of view
elements.label: text

elements.char: (FOV) placements between subjects, signal-to-noise ratio levels and mild slice resolution changes (i.e. compar-
elements.label: text

elements.char: ing healthy subjects to patients).

elements.char: The underlying assumption of spatio-temporal sharing in 3D cardiac CINE is that it contains a rich amount
elements.label: text

elements.char: of redundancy in a local neighborhood along all temporal directions (cardiac phases) which can be exploited.
elements.label: text

elements.char: We assume that similar structures exist in different cardiac phases, but at different spatial locations around a
elements.label: text

elements.char: certain neighborhood of a given voxel. Therefore, spatial receptive field can be limited whereas temporal cover-
elements.label: text

elements.char: age should span the entire cardiac cycle. Encoding and decoding branches in the 4D UNet of CINENet increase
elements.label: text

elements.char: receptive fields while allowing for relatively small convolutional kernels. We achieved a receptive field coverage
elements.label: text

elements.char: of 33% in spatial and 100% in temporal direction, reflecting a spatially confined but full temporal information
elements.label: text

elements.char: sharing from all cardiac phases.
elements.label: text

elements.char: We used separable rectified linear (ReLU) activation functions on real and imaginary dimensions after each
elements.label: text

elements.char: convolutional kernel yielding good performance and stable convergence. Further activation functions such as
elements.label: text

elements.char: cardioid
elements.label: text

elements.char: , are conceivable but demand a careful reparameterization of the network. Batch normalization was
elements.label: text

elements.char: used as it provided improved edge delineation and less blurring in the reconstructed images in comparison to
elements.label: text

elements.char: instance normalization or omitting normalization layers. However, further comparisons in a larger cohort would
elements.label: text

elements.char: be required to conclude the best performing combination of activation and normalization. We used SENSE-based
elements.label: text

elements.char: multi-coil data consistency blocks between UNet stages to ensure data fidelity. We formulated the data consist-
elements.label: text

elements.char: ency as proximal mapping step with a fixed regularization weighting which we can treat as a layer operation with
elements.label: text

elements.char: forward and backward (gradient backpropagation) pass.

elements.char: The undersampled 3D CINE data requires a joint 4D processing of the data. Previously proposed architectures
elements.label: text

elements.char: for 2D dynamic imaging operate on 2D
elements.label: text

elements.char: time and are hence not applicable due to the 4D nature of the data.
elements.label: text

elements.char: Furthermore, 2D CINE data cannot be leveraged as resolution, contrast, undersampled phase-encoding direc-
elements.label: text

elements.char: tions and sampling trajectories are different. Hence, visual artifact appearance will differ. If slicing of the short
elements.label: text

elements.char: axis 3D images along the fully sampled frequency direction (vertical long axis) is conducted, the data would lose
elements.label: text

elements.char: the 3D spatial relationship and the ability to resolve vertical long axis motion, i.e. only a few of the resulting 2D
elements.label: text

elements.char: horizontal long axis slices would contain the heart and reconstruction of the dynamic through-plane (vertical
elements.label: text

elements.char: long axis) motion would be impaired. Cropping of the 4D volume into smaller chunks would hence (a) loose
elements.label: text

elements.char: dynamic information if cropped along temporal dimension or (b) demand consideration of band-pass filtering
elements.label: text

elements.char: in data
elements.label: text

elements.char: consistency
elements.label: text

elements.char: implying a more complicated data fidelity block if cropped along spatial dimension. The
